Title: PlanType
Body: A strategy plan takes its cycle from the strategy packages.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Plant
Body: The plant determines which work centres and task lists are available.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Status
Body: New, Change or Delete - what this request should do to the plan in SAP.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Cycle
Body: How often the plan calls an order.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Unit
Body: DAY, WK, MON or YR - or H for a counter-based plan.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: SchedInd
Body: Time - key date calls on the same date every year. Use it when the plan calls in early January.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: StatutorySortField
Body: Only fill this in if the inspection has its own statutory sort field.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ItemShortText
Body: Becomes the heading of the maintenance order. Describe the task, not the plan. Max 40 characters.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: FunctionalLocation
Body: Be as specific as possible, ideally down to component level. This is where the cost is posted.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ObjectList
Body: Must start at the same two-letter level as the reference object.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: MainWorkCenter
Body: If external suppliers are used, choose *SUP.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Revision
Body: REV means the task is done during the outage. First call is then fixed to 01/01.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: OrstedResponsible
Body: The person responsible. Defaults to you.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: Initials
Body: Initials of the person responsible, e.g. NIJUJ.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ItemLongText
Body: Describe the scope and what it takes to do the job safely. It is the first thing the technician sees in the order.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: plan
Heading: The plan text
Body: Always starts with the plant code (AVV, SKV, SSV ...), so the plan can be found when you cannot search by plant or functional location.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: plan
Heading: Call horizon
Body: The number of WORKING DAYS the generated order stays on the job list before basic finish is reached. Set from the cycle. Outage work uses 65 FCD.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: plan
Heading: Scheduling period
Body: How far ahead the calls are visible. Minimum 2 years, because the cost simulation in the BI report depends on it.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: plan
Heading: Sort field
Body: Used ONLY for statutory inspections (activity type 110/115). If Ladders is selected, EVERY item in the plan must be a statutory ladder inspection.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: plan
Heading: Outage work
Body: Tasks carried out during the annual outage are marked REV and called on 1/1.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: item
Heading: The long text
Body: The FIRST thing the maintenance crew sees in the generated order. Describe the scope. If cleaning, a hole watch, a crane, scaffolding or barriers are needed, say so briefly.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: item
Heading: The reference object
Body: Where the cost is posted. Give the functional location down to component level. If there are objects on the object list it can be less specific - but at least the two-letter level, e.g. SKV40 EB.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: item
Heading: The object list
Body: Cost center and business area must be the same for every functional location on the list. This does not apply to safety valves and pipe runs. For statutory inspection of pressure equipment: ONE functional location per item, object list empty.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: item
Heading: Activity types
Body: 101 preventive - 102 predetermined - 110 statutory inspection - 115 regulatory condition - 120 running, max 1 year - 130 cleaning - 160 lubrication. If 110 or 115 is used, the applicable legislation MUST be referenced.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: item
Heading: Priority
Body: Follows the activity matrix: red for 110/115 or safety critical equipment (SCEq), blue for 120, otherwise yellow.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ops
Heading: Split the job where there is a pause
Body: Scaffolding up and scaffolding down are two operations. Removing and refitting insulation are two. Otherwise the WOS app cannot show the sequence correctly.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ops
Heading: Chronological order
Body: Operations must run 0010, 0020, 0030 in the order the work is carried out, so the graphical view in WOS reflects the job.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ops
Heading: Every operation needs a time and manning estimate
Body: Work is the total number of man-hours. No. is the number of people, 1 is the default. SAP calculates Duration itself.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: ops
Heading: Control keys
Body: ZB01 internal *SUP, not counted in scheduling - PM01 internal work centres - PM02 external *LEV, a requisition is raised - PM03 framework agreement supplier on the service catalogue. The main responsible work centre must sit on operation 0010.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: pkg
Heading: The packages belong to the task list
Body: In SAP the strategy owns the packages, the task list owns the operation to package allocation, and the maintenance plan points at both.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: pkg
Heading: Hierarchy
Body: A hierarchical strategy such as 1-3-6-12 means the monthly job is also done at the quarterly and annual inspection. A rotating strategy such as year 1-2-3 does not - there each package must be ticked on its own.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre

Title: pkg
Heading: Every operation needs at least one package
Body: An operation without a package is never carried out. A package without operations calls an empty order.
Author: 21: Peter Bjerre
